On every finite label or root component the Gram determinant is a unit of $A_0$, the $A_0$-pairing is perfect and $\mathcal L^\vee=\mathcal L$. Moreover $\mathcal L=\{x:\langle x,x\rangle\in A_0\}$ inside the field scalar extension of the lattice. These are consequences after the grand loop, not prerequisites for it. Let $U_q^-=\bigoplus_{\nu\in Q_+}U_q^-[-\nu]$ be the negative half of the
Drinfeld-Jimbo algebra of a finite symmetrizable Cartan datum with $a_{ii}=2$
([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]],
[[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]), with skew derivations
$e_i',e_i''$ ([[def-kashiwara-skew-derivations-on-the-negative-quantum-half]]),
and let $(\ ,\ )$ be a bilinear form on $U_q^-$.

(i) **Existence and symmetry.** A bilinear form with $(1,1)=1$ and
$(F_iP,Q)=(P,e_i'(Q))$ for all $i,P,Q$ exists on $U_q^-$; every normalized
homogeneous form satisfying these conditions is symmetric; and by the
uniqueness of [[def-the-lusztig-kashiwara-bilinear-form-on-the-negative-quantum-half]]
there is exactly one such form. No separate right-adjunction formula for
$(P,QF_i)$ is asserted: in the rank-one subalgebra a formula
$(P,QF_i)=c\,(e_i''P,Q)$ with constant $c$ is false, as the explicit values in
(iv) show.

(ii) **Orthogonality.** $(U_q^-[-\nu],U_q^-[-\mu])=0$ whenever $\nu\ne\mu$.

(iii) **Nondegeneracy.** For every $0\ne x\in U_q^-$ there is $y\in U_q^-$ with
$(x,y)\ne0$; equivalently, the restriction of the form to each
finite-dimensional graded piece $U_q^-[-\nu]$ is nondegenerate.

(iv) **Integrality on the word lattice.** Let $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$
([[def-the-laurent-polynomial-ring]]) and let $W\subseteq U_A^-$ be the
$A$-span of the monomials $F_{i_1}\cdots F_{i_k}$ ($k\ge0$). Then
$W\subseteq U_A^-$ (because $F_i^k=[k]_i!F_i^{(k)}$ and $[k]_i!\in A$), and
$(W,W)\subseteq A$. On the larger divided-power lattice $U_A^-$ the form is
*not* $A$-valued: in the rank-one subalgebra generated by a single $F_i$ one
has, for all $a,b\ge0$,
$$(F_i^{(a)},F_i^{(b)})=\delta_{ab}\frac{q_i^{-a(a-1)/2}}{[a]_i!}=\delta_{ab}\frac{1}{[a]_{q_i^2}!},$$
in particular $(F_i^{(2)},F_i^{(2)})=1/(1+q_i^2)\notin A$; here
$[a]_{q_i^2}!=\prod_{m=1}^a(1+q_i^2+\cdots+q_i^{2(m-1)})$. Globally, with
$A_{\mathrm{loc}}=A[s^{-1}:s\in S]$, the localization of $A$ inverting the
multiplicative set $S=\{[r]_i!:i\in I,r\ge1\}$ (equivalently inverting the
Gaussian factorials $[r]_{q_i^2}!$), one has
$(U_A^-,U_A^-)\subseteq A_{\mathrm{loc}}$: divided-power words are word
vectors divided by finite products of these factorials. This is an exact
denominator bound, not an $A$-integrality assertion on $U_A^-$ in this
normalization.

Let $L_{\mathbb Z}(\infty)=U_A^-\cap\mathcal L(\infty)$ be the integral residue lattice of [[def-integral-residue-lattices-of-the-negative-half-and-highest-weight-modules]], with $L_{\mathbb Z}/qL_{\mathbb Z}\to\mathcal L(\infty)/q\mathcal L(\infty)$ the canonical injection. Then the image of this injection is exactly $\bigoplus_{b\in\mathcal B(\infty)}\mathbb Z b$; in particular $L_{\mathbb Z}/qL_{\mathbb Z}$ is a free $\mathbb Z$-module with basis $\mathcal B(\infty)$, and after tensoring with $\mathbb Q$ it is the full rational crystal space $\mathbb Q\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\bigoplus_b\mathbb Zb=\mathcal L(\infty)/q\mathcal L(\infty)$.

The normalized Kashiwara half form of [[thm-the-negative-half-bilinear-form-is-symmetric-nondegenerate-and-integral]] takes values on $U_A^-$ in $K_{\mathbb Z}=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1},(1-q^{2n})^{-1}:n\ge1]$ and on $L_{\mathbb Z}$ in $A_{\mathbb Z}=\mathbb Z[q,(1-q^{2n})^{-1}:n\ge1]$; consequently its residue pairing on $L_{\mathbb Z}/qL_{\mathbb Z}$ is $\mathbb Z$-valued. In the residue basis $\mathcal B(\infty)$ the coefficients of an integral element are its integer pairings with the basis vectors, and the elements of $L_{\mathbb Z}$ of norm $1$ are exactly $\mathcal B(\infty)\cup(-\mathcal B(\infty))$. The Kashiwara operators $\tilde e_i,\tilde f_i$ preserve $L_{\mathbb Z}$, hence induce endomorphisms of the integral residue subgroup. No $A$-module structure on $L_{\mathbb Z}$, no identification of the integral residue with the rational residue as a $\mathbb Z$-module, and no unsigned norm-$1$ characterization is asserted; the module integral residue basis is established only in the globalization theorem of this page.

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum for a quantum
group with $a_{ii}=2$ for all $i$
([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]), let
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be its Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra
([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]) with $q_i=q^{d_i}$ and
$K_i=K_{d_ih_i}$, and set

$$A:=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]\ \subseteq\ \mathbb Q(q),$$

the image of the Laurent polynomial ring $\Lambda_1=\mathbb Z[t]_{S}$ of
[[def-the-laurent-polynomial-ring]] under the unital ring homomorphism sending
$t$ to the indeterminate $q$; this homomorphism is injective and $A$ is a
subring of $\mathbb Q(q)$ (Verification, step 1.1). We work over this
commutative domain $A$ inside the field $\mathbb Q(q)$.

For $i\in I$, $c\in\mathbb Z$ and $t\ge0$ define the **toral quantum binomial**

$$T_{i,c,t}:=\begin{bmatrix}K_i;c\\ t\end{bmatrix}:=\prod_{s=1}^{t}\frac{K_iq_i^{\,c-s+1}-K_i^{-1}q_i^{\,-c+s-1}}{q_i^{\,s}-q_i^{\,-s}}\in U_q(\mathfrak g),$$

the empty product being $T_{i,c,0}:=1$. Each factor is defined in
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$ because $q_i^{\,s}-q_i^{\,-s}\ne0$ for $s\ge1$
([[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]), so
$T_{i,c,t}$ is a polynomial in $K_i^{\pm1}$ with coefficients in $\mathbb Q(q)$;
in particular all $T_{i,c,t}$ commute with the $K_h$ and with one another
(Verification, step 2.1).

The **Lusztig divided-power integral form** is the $A$-subalgebra

$$U_A:=\bigl\langle E_i^{(r)},\ F_i^{(r)},\ K_h^{\pm1},\ T_{i,c,t}\ \colon\ i\in I,\ r,t\ge0,\ c\in\mathbb Z,\ h\in P^{\vee}\bigr\rangle\ \subseteq\ U_q(\mathfrak g),$$

where $x^{(r)}=x^r/[r]_i!$ are the divided powers of
[[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]. Write $U_A^\pm$
for the $A$-subalgebras generated by the $E_i^{(r)}$ and by the $F_i^{(r)}$,
and $U_A^0$ for the one generated by the $K_h^{\pm1}$ and the $T_{i,c,t}$.

Then:

(i) $U_A$ contains $E_i=E_i^{(1)}$, $F_i=F_i^{(1)}$ and all $K_h$;

(ii) $U_A$ is a root-graded $A$-subalgebra of the root-graded
$\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ ([[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]):
with $U_A[\beta]:=U_A\cap U_q(\mathfrak g)[\beta]$ one has
$U_A=\bigoplus_{\beta\in Q}U_A[\beta]$, each $U_A[\beta]$ is an $A$-submodule,
and $U_A^\pm,U_A^0$ are graded in the same way;

(iii) $U_A\otimes_A\mathbb Q(q)\cong U_q(\mathfrak g)$ canonically, i.e. the
$\mathbb Q(q)$-span of $U_A$ is all of $U_q(\mathfrak g)$.

The shifted binomials $T_{i,c,t}$ with $c\ne0$ are included because the
divided-power reordering identity of
[[lem-divided-power-and-toral-quantum-binomial-reordering-identities]] has
coefficients $T_{i,2t-a-b,t}$ with a nonconstant index; the specializations at
$q=1$ of these elements are computed in
[[lem-q-one-toral-specialization-identifies-the-classical-cartan-generators]],
and the integral triangular decomposition and the specialization are treated
only after this definition.

No freeness of $U_A$ or of its parts over $A$, no independence of the listed
generators, and no triangularity of the products of the three parts is asserted
here. In particular $A$ is not a principal ideal domain (Verification, step
7.1), so no torsion-free-to-free inference over $A$ is permitted anywhere on
this page.

derivations.claim: **$\star$ is a well-defined anti-involution.** The assignment $F_i\mapsto F_i$ extended antimultiplicatively is defined on the free algebra, and applying it to a negative Serre relation $\sum_r(-1)^r\binom{1-a_{ij}}{r}_iF_i^{1-a_{ij}-r}F_jF_i^r=0$ and reversing the order of each monomial gives $\sum_r(-1)^r\binom{1-a_{ij}}{r}_iF_i^{r}F_jF_i^{1-a_{ij}-r}$, which is the same sum after the substitution $r\mapsto1-a_{ij}-r$ and the exact symmetry $\binom{m}{r}_i=\binom{m}{m-r}_i$ of the Gaussian binomials. Hence $\star$ descends to $U_q^-$, fixes $F_i$, and is an anti-involution: it reverses words and its square is the identity.

**Integral and bar compatibility.** Since $\star$ fixes each divided power $F_i^{(r)}$ (it fixes $F_i$ and the scalar $[r]_i!$), it maps each generator of $U_A^-$ to a generator, so $\star(U_A^-)=U_A^-$. It commutes with $\psi$ because both are $\mathbb Q(q)$-semilinear, $\star$ fixes $q$ while $\psi$ sends $q\mapsto q^{-1}$, and on generators $\psi\star(F_i)=\psi(F_i)=F_i=\star\psi(F_i)$.

**Isometry for the half form.** Write $P=F_{i_1}\cdots F_{i_r}$, $Q=F_{j_1}\cdots F_{j_s}$ as words. Reversing both words, $P^\star=F_{i_r}\cdots F_{i_1}$, $Q^\star=F_{j_s}\cdots F_{j_1}$, and the word Gram formula of [F1] expands both $B(P,Q)$ and $B(P^\star,Q^\star)$ as sums over bijections between matched colors with the same crossing exponents read backwards; reversing a permutation preserves the weight and the crossing number, so the two sums are termwise equal. Hence $B(P^\star,Q^\star)=B(P,Q)$ on words and, by bilinearity and descent through the Serre ideal, on all of $U_q^-$.

**Lattice stability.** For $P\in\mathcal L(\infty)$ one has $B(P^\star,P^\star)=B(P,P)\in A_0$ by step 2.1 and the norm characterization of [F1]; hence $P^\star\in\mathcal L(\infty)$ and $\star$ preserves $\mathcal L(\infty)$. It preserves $U_A^-$ by step 1.2, so it preserves $L_{\mathbb Z}=U_A^-\cap\mathcal L(\infty)$; since it commutes with $\psi$ and $\psi(L_{\mathbb Z})=L_{\mathbb Z}^-$, it also preserves the bar lattice $L_{\mathbb Z}^-$.

**The signed residue permutation.** For $x\in L_{\mathbb Z}$ with residue $\sum_ba_bb$, the residue of $x^\star$ is $\sum_ba_b'b$ where the coefficients are determined by the orthonormal residue pairing; because the residue pairing is invariant under $\star$ by step 2.1, $a_b'=a_b$ up to the index permutation induced by a signed bijection of the basis: by the signed norm characterization of [F2], if $x$ has norm $1$ then $x^\star$ has norm $1$, so $\star$ maps the set of signed basis classes $\mathcal B(\infty)\cup(-\mathcal B(\infty))$ to itself, permuting it.

**Conclusion.** Steps 1.1–1.2 prove that $\star$ is an anti-involution preserving $U_A^-$ and commuting with bar, step 2.1 proves that it is an isometry of the normalized half form, step 3.1 proves preservation of $\mathcal L(\infty)$, $L_{\mathbb Z}$ and $L_{\mathbb Z}^-$, and step 4.1 gives the signed permutation of the integral crystal residue. No unsigned star-crystal theorem is asserted.

Let $U_q^-$ be the negative half of the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra with its
Kashiwara skew derivations $e_i',e_i''$
([[def-kashiwara-skew-derivations-on-the-negative-quantum-half]]), let
$A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ and let $U_A^-$ be the divided-power half generated by
the $F_i^{(r)}$ ([[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]]). Then:

(i) $e_i'$ preserves $U_A^-$: $e_i'(U_A^-)\subseteq U_A^-$.

(ii) Define, for $x\in U_q^-$,
$$P_ix:=\sum_{n\ge0}(-1)^nq_i^{-n(n-1)/2}\,F_i^{(n)}(e_i')^n x,$$
the sum being finite on each $x$ because $e_i'$ is locally nilpotent, and the
powers $(e_i')^n$ being ordinary, not divided, powers of the derivation. Then
$P_i$ is a well-defined $\mathbb Q(q)$-linear map with $e_i'P_i=0$ that fixes
$\ker e_i'$ pointwise and annihilates $F_iU_q^-$; hence
$U_q^-=\ker e_i'\oplus F_iU_q^-$ and $P_i$ is the projection onto $\ker e_i'$
along $F_iU_q^-$.

(iii) Every $x\in U_A^-$ has a unique finite expansion
$$x=\sum_{n\ge0}F_i^{(n)}x_n,\qquad e_i'x_n=0,$$
with $x_n=q_i^{n(n-1)/2}P_i(e_i')^nx\in U_A^-$ for every $n$; the sum is finite
because $(e_i')^nx=0$ for large $n$. Consequently the string operators
$\tilde e_i\bigl(\sum_nF_i^{(n)}x_n\bigr):=\sum_{n\ge1}F_i^{(n-1)}x_n$ and
$\tilde f_i\bigl(\sum_nF_i^{(n)}x_n\bigr):=\sum_{n\ge0}F_i^{(n+1)}x_n$
preserve $U_A^-$.

No global $A$-basis and no freeness of $U_A^-$ over $A$ is assumed or asserted.

Let $U_q^-$ be the negative half of the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra with its skew derivations $e_i',e_i'':U_q^-\to U_q^-$ ([[def-kashiwara-skew-derivations-on-the-negative-quantum-half]], [[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]), fix $i\in I$, and write $f_i^{(n)}=F_i^n/[n]_i!$ for the divided powers ([[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]). Then:

(i) $e_i'$ is locally nilpotent on $U_q^-$, and the endomorphism
$$P_i:=\sum_{m\ge0}(-1)^mq_i^{-m(m-1)/2}F_i^{(m)}e_i'^{\,m}\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb Q(q)}(U_q^-)$$
is well defined (each sum is finite on each element) and is the projection onto $\operatorname{Ker}e_i'$ along $f_iU_q^-$. In particular $e_i'P_i=0$, $P_iF_i=0$, $P_i^2=P_i$, $P_iu=u$ for $u\in\operatorname{Ker}e_i'$, and
$$U_q^-=\operatorname{Ker}e_i'\oplus f_iU_q^-.$$

(ii) Every $u\in U_q^-$ has a unique $i$-string decomposition
$$u=\sum_{n\ge0}f_i^{(n)}u_n,\qquad u_n\in\operatorname{Ker}e_i',\qquad u_n=0\ \text{for }n\gg0,$$
and the components are given by $u_n=q_i^{n(n-1)/2}P_ie_i'^{\,n}u$.

(iii) The **Kashiwara operators on the negative half**, defined on the string decomposition by
$$\tilde e_iu:=\sum_{n\ge1}f_i^{(n-1)}u_n,\qquad \tilde f_iu:=\sum_{n\ge0}f_i^{(n+1)}u_n,$$
are $\mathbb Q(q)$-linear endomorphisms of $U_q^-$ with $\tilde e_i\tilde f_i=\operatorname{id}_{U_q^-}$; $\tilde e_iu=0$ if and only if $u\in\operatorname{Ker}e_i'$; $\tilde f_i$ is injective and $\tilde f_i(1)=F_i$. Both operators preserve the root grading and shift its degree by $\mp\alpha_i$, that is $\tilde e_i(U_q^-[-\nu])\subseteq U_q^-[-\nu+\alpha_i]$ and $\tilde f_i(U_q^-[-\nu])\subseteq U_q^-[-\nu-\alpha_i]$.

No choice principle is used. Here $e_i'^{\,n}$ denotes the ordinary $n$-fold power of the derivation, not its divided power. The same projector and every string coefficient preserve the $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ divided-power lattice $U_A^-$ ([[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]]), as proved by the integral skew-string supplier; this does not assert that lattice's freeness.

Let $\mathcal L(\infty)\subseteq U_q^-$ and $\mathcal B(\infty)\subseteq\mathcal L(\infty)/q\mathcal L(\infty)$ be the Kashiwara lattice and generating set of [[def-kashiwara-lattices-lambda-and-infinity]], with the Kashiwara operators $\tilde e_i,\tilde f_i$ on $U_q^-$ of [[thm-the-i-string-decomposition-of-the-negative-half]](iii).

(i) $(\mathcal L(\infty),\mathcal B(\infty))$ is a crystal basis of $U_q^-$ in the sense of [[def-crystal-lattice-and-crystal-basis]]: $\mathcal L(\infty)$ is a free $A_0$-submodule with $U_q^-\cong\mathbb Q(q)\otimes_{A_0}\mathcal L(\infty)$, stable under $\tilde e_i$ and $\tilde f_i$; and $\mathcal B(\infty)$ is a $\mathbb Q$-basis of $\mathcal L(\infty)/q\mathcal L(\infty)$ satisfying $\tilde e_i\mathcal B(\infty)\subseteq\mathcal B(\infty)\cup\{0\}$, $\tilde f_i\mathcal B(\infty)\subseteq\mathcal B(\infty)$, and $\tilde f_ib=b'$ if and only if $b=\tilde e_ib'$ for all $b,b'\in\mathcal B(\infty)$.

(ii) The root-graded components are free: $\mathcal L(\infty)=\bigoplus_{\nu\in Q_+}\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\nu}$ and each $\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\nu}$ is a free $A_0$-module of rank $\#\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\nu}=\dim_{\mathbb Q(q)}U_q^-[-\nu]$.

(iii) For every $\lambda\in P^+$ the projection $\pi_\lambda(P)=Pv_\lambda$ maps $\mathcal B(\infty)$ onto $\mathcal B(\lambda)\cup\{0\}$, and the compatibility statements of [[lem-crystal-operators-commute-with-highest-weight-projection-modulo-q]] hold: $\pi_\lambda(\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha})=\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$, $\{b\in\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\alpha}:\pi_\lambda(b)\neq0\}\cong\mathcal B(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$, $\tilde f_i\pi_\lambda=\pi_\lambda\tilde f_i$ and $\tilde e_i\pi_\lambda(b)=\pi_\lambda(\tilde e_ib)$ whenever $\pi_\lambda(b)\neq0$.

(iv) The root-graded crystal has finite $\varepsilon_i$ on each element, formal $\varphi_i=\varepsilon_i+\langle h_i,\mathrm{wt}\rangle$, and actual lowering length $\ell_i^-=\infty$. Every $\tilde f_i$-iterate is nonzero because $\tilde e_i\tilde f_i=\mathrm{id}$ holds on its lattice and residue. Thus it is the infinite lowering crystal of the unit, with the negative-half convention of the crystal-graph definition.

**Choice.** The axiom of choice is declared via [[def-axiom-of-choice]] and enters only through the grand loop: the partial-inverse axiom in (i) uses clause J(r) of [[thm-grand-loop-existence-of-highest-weight-crystal-bases]], whose proof consumes the AC-dependent form comparison of the negative-half form. Let $\lambda\in P^+$ and let $\mathcal L(\lambda),\mathcal B(\lambda),\mathcal L(\infty),\mathcal B(\infty)$ be the lattices and bases of [[def-kashiwara-lattices-lambda-and-infinity]], with $\pi_\lambda:U_q^-\to V(\lambda)$, $P\mapsto Pv_\lambda$, and Kashiwara operators $\tilde e_i,\tilde f_i$. Clauses (a), (b) and (d) are themselves choice-free.

Let $L_{\mathbb Z}(\infty)=U_A^-\cap\mathcal L(\infty)$ be the integral residue lattice of [[def-integral-residue-lattices-of-the-negative-half-and-highest-weight-modules]], with $L_{\mathbb Z}/qL_{\mathbb Z}\to\mathcal L(\infty)/q\mathcal L(\infty)$ the canonical injection. Then the image of this injection is exactly $\bigoplus_{b\in\mathcal B(\infty)}\mathbb Z b$; in particular $L_{\mathbb Z}/qL_{\mathbb Z}$ is a free $\mathbb Z$-module with basis $\mathcal B(\infty)$, and after tensoring with $\mathbb Q$ it is the full rational crystal space $\mathbb Q\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\bigoplus_b\mathbb Zb=\mathcal L(\infty)/q\mathcal L(\infty)$.

The normalized Kashiwara half form of [[thm-the-negative-half-bilinear-form-is-symmetric-nondegenerate-and-integral]] takes values on $U_A^-$ in $K_{\mathbb Z}=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1},(1-q^{2n})^{-1}:n\ge1]$ and on $L_{\mathbb Z}$ in $A_{\mathbb Z}=\mathbb Z[q,(1-q^{2n})^{-1}:n\ge1]$; consequently its residue pairing on $L_{\mathbb Z}/qL_{\mathbb Z}$ is $\mathbb Z$-valued. In the residue basis $\mathcal B(\infty)$ the coefficients of an integral element are its integer pairings with the basis vectors, and the elements of $L_{\mathbb Z}$ of norm $1$ are exactly $\mathcal B(\infty)\cup(-\mathcal B(\infty))$. The Kashiwara operators $\tilde e_i,\tilde f_i$ preserve $L_{\mathbb Z}$, hence induce endomorphisms of the integral residue subgroup. No $A$-module structure on $L_{\mathbb Z}$, no identification of the integral residue with the rational residue as a $\mathbb Z$-module, and no unsigned norm-$1$ characterization is asserted; the module integral residue basis is established only in the globalization theorem of this page.

Fix a symmetrizable Cartan datum and $i\in I$, and use the conventions of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]. Write $C_{m,r}:=\binom{m}{r}_i$, with $C_{m,r}=0$ when $r<0$ or $r>m$.

(i) **Pascal recurrences.** For $m\ge1$ and every integer $r$,

$$C_{m,r}=q_i^{-r}C_{m-1,r}+q_i^{m-r}C_{m-1,r-1}=q_i^rC_{m-1,r}+q_i^{r-m}C_{m-1,r-1}.$$

(ii) **Symmetry.** For $0\le r\le m$, $C_{m,r}=C_{m,m-r}$.

(iii) **Gauss product formula.** For every $N\ge0$, in the polynomial ring $\mathbb Q(q)[z]$,

$$\prod_{j=0}^{N-1}(1+q_i^{2j}z)=\sum_{r=0}^{N}q_i^{r(N-1)}C_{N,r}z^r.$$

Consequently, for $N\ge1$,

$$\sum_{r=0}^{N}(-1)^rq_i^{r(N-1)}C_{N,r}=0.$$

(iv) **Integrality.** For $0\le r\le m$,

$$C_{m,r}\in q_i^{-r(m-r)}\mathbb Z[q_i^2]\subseteq\mathbb Z[q_i^{\pm1}].$$

Thus every Gaussian quotient is a Laurent polynomial in $q_i$ with integer coefficients, and the Pascal recurrences hold in that Laurent polynomial ring.

Let $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra of
[[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]], with its generated
subalgebras $U_q^-,U_q^0,U_q^+$ and root gradings
$U_q^-=\bigoplus_{\nu\in Q_+}U_q^-[-\nu]$ of
[[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]
($Q_+=\bigoplus_i\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\alpha_i$, height $\operatorname{ht}$ of
[[def-kac-moody-root-lattice-height-and-positive-cone]]). Fix $i\in I$ and
write $K_i:=K_{d_ih_i}$, so that $K_iF_jK_i^{-1}=q_i^{-a_{ij}}F_j$ and
$q_i-q_i^{-1}\ne0$.

For every $P\in U_q^-$ there exist unique elements $Q,R\in U_q^-$ with

$$E_iP-PE_i=\frac{K_iQ-K_i^{-1}R}{q_i-q_i^{-1}}.$$

Define the **Kashiwara skew derivations** $e_i',e_i'':U_q^-\to U_q^-$ by

$$e_i'(P):=R\qquad\text{and}\qquad e_i''(P):=Q .$$

Thus $e_i'$ is the operator whose value is the coefficient of $K_i^{-1}$ and
$e_i''$ is the operator whose value is the coefficient of $K_i$ in the
commutator with $E_i$. The maps have the following properties, all proved in
the Verification below.

(a) $e_i'$ and $e_i''$ are $\mathbb Q(q)$-linear, vanish on $1$, and
$e_i'(F_j)=e_i''(F_j)=\delta_{ij}$ for all $j\in I$.

(b) (Twisted Leibniz rules) For homogeneous $x,y\in U_q^-$, with the actual
weight $\operatorname{wt}(x)\in Q$ of [[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]],
$$e_i'(xy)=e_i'(x)y+q_i^{\langle\operatorname{wt}(x),h_i\rangle}x\,e_i'(y),\qquad e_i''(xy)=e_i''(x)y+q_i^{-\langle\operatorname{wt}(x),h_i\rangle}x\,e_i''(y).$$

(c) (Commutation with the generators) For all $j\in I$ and all $y\in U_q^-$,
$$e_i'(F_jy)=q_i^{-a_{ij}}F_j\,e_i'(y)+\delta_{ij}y,\qquad e_i''(F_jy)=q_i^{a_{ij}}F_j\,e_i''(y)+\delta_{ij}y,$$

equivalently $e_i'F_j=q_i^{-a_{ij}}F_je_i'+\delta_{ij}$ and
$e_i''F_j=q_i^{a_{ij}}F_je_i''+\delta_{ij}$ as operators on $U_q^-$.

(d) (Grading, height and nilpotence) For every $\nu\in Q_+$,

$$e_i'\bigl(U_q^-[-\nu]\bigr),\ e_i''\bigl(U_q^-[-\nu]\bigr)\ \subseteq\ U_q^-[ -(\nu-\alpha_i)],$$

the right-hand side being $0$ when $\nu-\alpha_i\notin Q_+$. In particular both
maps raise the actual weight by $\alpha_i$, lower the positive height by one,
and are locally nilpotent: $(e_i')^{k}(P)=(e_i'')^{k}(P)=0$ for $k$ larger than
the height of the degree of a homogeneous $P$.

(e) (Bar compatibility) Let $\psi$ be the semilinear algebra involution
$q\mapsto q^{-1}$, $E_i\mapsto E_i$, $F_i\mapsto F_i$, $K_h\mapsto K_{-h}$ of
[[lem-quantum-serre-relations-are-stable-under-the-chevalley-involutions]].
Then $e_i''=\psi\,e_i'\,\psi$ on $U_q^-$.

The commutator construction also fixes the orientation: the
$K_i^{-1}$-coefficient is $e_i'$ and the $K_i$-coefficient is $e_i''$. The
twists $q_i^{\pm\langle\operatorname{wt}(x),h_i\rangle}$ in (b) are the twists
of the corresponding coefficient maps of the negative-half coproduct in the
source's dictionary; the explicit commutator computation used here is the
definition of record, and no imaginary-simple-root convention is needed, since
every Cartan datum of this library has $a_{ii}=2$.

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum for a quantum
group with $a_{ii}=2$ for all $i$
([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]), let
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be its Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra
([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]) with $q_i=q^{d_i}$ and
$K_i=K_{d_ih_i}$, and set

$$A:=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]\ \subseteq\ \mathbb Q(q),$$

the image of the Laurent polynomial ring $\Lambda_1=\mathbb Z[t]_{S}$ of
[[def-the-laurent-polynomial-ring]] under the unital ring homomorphism sending
$t$ to the indeterminate $q$; this homomorphism is injective and $A$ is a
subring of $\mathbb Q(q)$ (Verification, step 1.1). We work over this
commutative domain $A$ inside the field $\mathbb Q(q)$.

For $i\in I$, $c\in\mathbb Z$ and $t\ge0$ define the **toral quantum binomial**

$$T_{i,c,t}:=\begin{bmatrix}K_i;c\\ t\end{bmatrix}:=\prod_{s=1}^{t}\frac{K_iq_i^{\,c-s+1}-K_i^{-1}q_i^{\,-c+s-1}}{q_i^{\,s}-q_i^{\,-s}}\in U_q(\mathfrak g),$$

the empty product being $T_{i,c,0}:=1$. Each factor is defined in
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$ because $q_i^{\,s}-q_i^{\,-s}\ne0$ for $s\ge1$
([[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]), so
$T_{i,c,t}$ is a polynomial in $K_i^{\pm1}$ with coefficients in $\mathbb Q(q)$;
in particular all $T_{i,c,t}$ commute with the $K_h$ and with one another
(Verification, step 2.1).

The **Lusztig divided-power integral form** is the $A$-subalgebra

$$U_A:=\bigl\langle E_i^{(r)},\ F_i^{(r)},\ K_h^{\pm1},\ T_{i,c,t}\ \colon\ i\in I,\ r,t\ge0,\ c\in\mathbb Z,\ h\in P^{\vee}\bigr\rangle\ \subseteq\ U_q(\mathfrak g),$$

where $x^{(r)}=x^r/[r]_i!$ are the divided powers of
[[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]. Write $U_A^\pm$
for the $A$-subalgebras generated by the $E_i^{(r)}$ and by the $F_i^{(r)}$,
and $U_A^0$ for the one generated by the $K_h^{\pm1}$ and the $T_{i,c,t}$.

Then:

(i) $U_A$ contains $E_i=E_i^{(1)}$, $F_i=F_i^{(1)}$ and all $K_h$;

(ii) $U_A$ is a root-graded $A$-subalgebra of the root-graded
$\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ ([[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]):
with $U_A[\beta]:=U_A\cap U_q(\mathfrak g)[\beta]$ one has
$U_A=\bigoplus_{\beta\in Q}U_A[\beta]$, each $U_A[\beta]$ is an $A$-submodule,
and $U_A^\pm,U_A^0$ are graded in the same way;

(iii) $U_A\otimes_A\mathbb Q(q)\cong U_q(\mathfrak g)$ canonically, i.e. the
$\mathbb Q(q)$-span of $U_A$ is all of $U_q(\mathfrak g)$.

The shifted binomials $T_{i,c,t}$ with $c\ne0$ are included because the
divided-power reordering identity of
[[lem-divided-power-and-toral-quantum-binomial-reordering-identities]] has
coefficients $T_{i,2t-a-b,t}$ with a nonconstant index; the specializations at
$q=1$ of these elements are computed in
[[lem-q-one-toral-specialization-identifies-the-classical-cartan-generators]],
and the integral triangular decomposition and the specialization are treated
only after this definition.

No freeness of $U_A$ or of its parts over $A$, no independence of the listed
generators, and no triangularity of the products of the three parts is asserted
here. In particular $A$ is not a principal ideal domain (Verification, step
7.1), so no torsion-free-to-free inference over $A$ is permitted anywhere on
this page.

Let $\lambda\in P^+$ and let $L(\lambda)$ be the simple integrable highest weight module with highest weight vector $v_\lambda$ ([[thm-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module-exists-and-is-unique]]); in this page we write $V(\lambda):=L(\lambda)$, following the notation of the crystal sources. Let $U_q^-$ be the negative half with its Kashiwara operators $\tilde e_i,\tilde f_i$ ([[thm-the-i-string-decomposition-of-the-negative-half]]), and let $A_0$ be the crystal limiting ring ([[def-the-local-ring-at-q-zero]]).

Define $\mathcal L(\lambda)$ to be the $A_0$-submodule of $V(\lambda)$ generated by all vectors $\tilde f_{i_1}\cdots\tilde f_{i_r}v_\lambda$ ($r\ge0$, $i_1,\dots,i_r\in I$), where for $r=0$ the vector is $v_\lambda$; and $\mathcal L(\infty)$ to be the $A_0$-submodule of $U_q^-$ generated by all $\tilde f_{i_1}\cdots\tilde f_{i_r}\mathbf 1$ ($r\ge0$), where $\mathbf 1$ is the unit of $U_q^-$. Here $\tilde f_i$ on $V(\lambda)$ are the module Kashiwara operators and $\tilde f_i$ on $U_q^-$ are the negative-half operators. Define
$$\mathcal B(\lambda):=\{\tilde f_{i_1}\cdots\tilde f_{i_r}v_\lambda+q\mathcal L(\lambda):r\ge0\}\setminus\{0\}\subseteq\mathcal L(\lambda)/q\mathcal L(\lambda),$$
$$\mathcal B(\infty):=\{\tilde f_{i_1}\cdots\tilde f_{i_r}\mathbf 1+q\mathcal L(\infty):r\ge0\}\setminus\{0\}\subseteq\mathcal L(\infty)/q\mathcal L(\infty).$$

Then, with $\pi_\lambda:U_q^-\to V(\lambda)$, $\pi_\lambda(P)=Pv_\lambda$:

(a) $\mathcal L(\lambda)=\bigoplus_{\mu\in P}\mathcal L(\lambda)_\mu$ with $\mathcal L(\lambda)_\mu=\mathcal L(\lambda)\cap V(\lambda)_\mu$, and $\mathcal L(\infty)=\bigoplus_{\nu\in Q_+}\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\nu}$ with $\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\nu}=\mathcal L(\infty)\cap U_q^-[-\nu]$; correspondingly $\mathcal B(\lambda)=\bigsqcup_\mu\mathcal B(\lambda)_\mu$ and $\mathcal B(\infty)=\bigsqcup_\nu\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\nu}$.

(b) $\tilde f_i\mathcal L(\lambda)\subseteq\mathcal L(\lambda)$ and $\tilde f_i\mathcal L(\infty)\subseteq\mathcal L(\infty)$.

(c) (Recursive spanning.) For $\alpha\in Q_+\setminus\{0\}$,
$$\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}=\sum_{i\in I}\tilde f_i\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha+\alpha_i},\qquad \mathcal B(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}=\Bigl(\bigcup_{i\in I}\tilde f_i\mathcal B(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha+\alpha_i}\Bigr)\setminus\{0\},$$
and the same formulas with $\mathcal L(\infty),\mathcal B(\infty)$. Each $\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$ and each $\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha}$ is generated over $A_0$ by finitely many monomials of total length at most $\operatorname{ht}(\alpha)$, hence is a finitely generated $A_0$-module.

No basis property, scalar-extension spanning or crystal-lattice property of $\mathcal L(\lambda)$ or $\mathcal L(\infty)$ is asserted here; these are conclusions of the grand loop. The script letters avoid the collision with the simple module $L(\lambda)$. No choice principle is used. Each fixed component is torsionfree inside a field vector space and generated by finitely many words of its fixed height, so it is free over the DVR $A_0$; its full field-span is proved later. The field map $\pi_\lambda$ is surjective, but exact equality on Kashiwara monomial generators is not asserted.

derivations.claim: **The integral string decomposition and projector.** For $u\in U_A^-$ the unique decomposition of [F2] has $u_l=q_i^{l(l-1)/2}P_i(e_i')^lu$ with $P_i=\sum_l(-1)^lq_i^{-l(l-1)/2}F_i^{(l)}(e_i')^l$, the powers of $e_i'$ being ordinary; by [F1] the coefficients $q_i^{\pm l(l-1)/2}$ and the operators $F_i^{(l)}$ and $(e_i')^l$ preserve $U_A^-$, so every $u_l$ lies in $U_A^-$.

**The finite Gaussian identity.** Put $z=q_i$, $Q=z^2$ and $H(t)=\prod_{j=1}^{n-1}(1-Q^{-j}t)\prod_{j=1}^{m-n}(1-Q^jt)$, a polynomial of degree $m-1$. For every polynomial of degree $\le m-1$ the finite $q$-binomial theorem of [F5] gives $\sum_{k=0}^m(-1)^kQ^{k(k-1)/2-k(m-1)}\binom{m}{k}_QH(Q^k)=0$: on the monomial $t^s$ the sum factors as $\prod_{j=0}^{m-1}(1-Q^{j+s-m+1})$, which contains the zero factor $j=m-1-s$. For $1\le k<n$ one has $H(Q^k)=0$; for $k\ge n$, $H(Q^k)/[(Q;Q)_{n-1}(Q;Q)_{m-n}]=\binom{k-1}{n-1}_Q\binom{m-n+k}{k}_Q$; and the $k=0$ term equals $(-1)^{n-1}Q^{-n(n-1)/2}$. Multiplying the vanishing sum by $(-1)^nQ^{n(n-1)/2}$ divided by the two factorials turns it into $\sum_{k=n}^m(-1)^{k-n}\binom{k-1}{k-n}_z\binom{m-n+k}{k}_z\binom{m}{k}_z=1$, using $\binom{a}{b}_z=z^{-b(a-b)}\binom{a}{b}_Q$ and the exponent identity $k(k-1)/2-k(m-1)+n(n-1)/2=-(k-n)(m-k)$.

**String ideals.** By [F2], $u\in F_i^nU_q^-$ if and only if $u_l=0$ for $l<n$; hence $I_{(i,n)}=U_A^-\cap F_i^nU_q^-$ equals $\bigoplus_{l\ge n}F_i^{(l)}(\ker e_i'\cap U_A^-)$ directly, and this equals the sum $\sum_{l\ge n}F_i^{(l)}U_A^-$ because $F_i^{(l)}U_A^-=F_i^{(l)}(\ker e_i'\cap U_A^-)\oplus F_i^{(l+1)}U_A^-$ by the same decomposition; the sum is not direct as written. Applying the $A$-linear projection $\pi_\lambda$ of [[def-integral-residue-lattices-of-the-negative-half-and-highest-weight-modules]] gives $J_{(i,n)}^A=\sum_{l\ge n}F_i^{(l)}V_A(\lambda)$, an $A$-submodule of the field subspace $F_i^nV(\lambda)$, with no $U_q$- or $U_A$-stability asserted.

**Boundary generation on a module lattice.** Let $u=F_i^{(m)}v$ with $e_i'v=0$ and $2m-n\ge0$, so that $m\ge n$; the rank-one divided-power formulas give $F_i^{(k)}E_i^{(k)}u=\binom{m-n+k}{k}_z\binom{m}{k}_zu$ for $k\le m$ and $0$ for $k>m$. Substituting step 1.2, the alternating sum of step (iv) is $u$: the coefficients are exactly those of the proved identity, with finite support because $k\le m$. Every $u\in(M_A)_\mu$ is a finite sum of such string vectors, and all operators and coefficients involved lie in $A$ and preserve $M_A$ ([[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]]), so $(M_A)_\mu=\sum_{k\ge n}F_i^{(k)}(M_A)_{\mu+k\alpha_i}$, with finiteness supplied by integrability.

**The integral residue of a string ideal.** Every word representative $\tilde f_{i_1}\cdots\tilde f_{i_r}\mathbf 1$ lies in $U_A^-\cap\mathcal L(\infty)=L_{\mathbb Z}$ by [F1] and [F3]; those whose words begin with $n$ letters equal to $i$ lie in $I_{(i,n)}^A\cap\mathcal L(\infty)$, and prepending $n$ copies of $i$ to the word of $b$ shows that the residue classes in $\mathcal B(\infty)\cap\tilde f_i^n\mathcal B(\infty)$ have integral representatives there. Conversely, if $x\in I_{(i,n)}^A\cap\mathcal L(\infty)$, then by [F2] its string expansion has no components of degree $<n$ along $i$, so by [F3] its residue lies in the span of $\mathcal B(\infty)\cap\tilde f_i^n\mathcal B(\infty)$; the residue basis being integral by [F4], the residue subgroup is exactly the free $\mathbb Z$-span of that subset, and the rational residue of $F_i^nU_q^-\cap\mathcal L(\infty)$ is its $\mathbb Q$-span.

(i) the image string ideal $J_{(i,n)}^A$ in each highest module $V(\lambda)$, with its rational zero- and infinity-chart intersections, is integrally balanced in degree $\lambda-\alpha$, and its balanced $\mathbb Z$-intersection maps isomorphically to the $\mathbb Z$-span of $\mathcal B_\lambda\cap\tilde f_i^n\mathcal B_\lambda$ in that degree;

(ii) the half ideal $I_{(i,n)}^A$ is integrally balanced in degree $-\alpha$, with balanced intersection mapping isomorphically to the $\mathbb Z$-span of $\mathcal B_\infty\cap\tilde f_i^n\mathcal B_\infty$; and

(iii) their Laurent extensions are free $A$-modules with the adapted global lifts.

Freeness, the chart intersections and the eventual module saturation $J_{(i,n)}^A=V_A(\lambda)\cap F_i^nV(\lambda)$ are conclusions, not hypotheses.

Let $V$ be finite-dimensional over $\mathbb Q(q)$, let $M\subset V$ be an $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-submodule spanning $V$, and let $L_0,L_\infty$ be full free $A_0$- and $A_\infty$-lattices in $V$. Write $E=M\cap L_0\cap L_\infty$ and use the balanced-triple language of [[def-balanced-triple-and-globalization-map]].

(1) If the canonical $\mathbb Z$-linear map $E\to(M\cap L_0)/(M\cap qL_0)$ is an isomorphism, then
$$M\cap L_0\cong\mathbb Z[q]\otimes_{\mathbb Z}E,\qquad M\cap L_\infty\cong\mathbb Z[q^{-1}]\otimes_{\mathbb Z}E,\qquad M\cong A\otimes_{\mathbb Z}E,$$
and the infinity residue map $E\to(M\cap L_\infty)/(M\cap q^{-1}L_\infty)$ is also an isomorphism; moreover $A_0\otimes_{\mathbb Z}E\cong L_0$ and $A_\infty\otimes_{\mathbb Z}E\cong L_\infty$ under the maps induced by inclusions. If $E$ has a finite $\mathbb Z$-basis, these are actual free bases of $M,L_0,L_\infty$ over $A,A_0,A_\infty$. No containment $M\subset L_0\cap L_\infty$ and no freeness of $M/E$ is assumed.

(2) If a $\mathbb Z$-module $F$ maps into $M\cap L_0\cap L_\infty$, generates $M$ over $A$, and maps injectively into both rational residues $L_0/qL_0$ and $L_\infty/q^{-1}L_\infty$, then $F\cong E\cong(M\cap L_0)/(M\cap qL_0)$.

(3) More generally, let $N\subset M$ be an $A$-submodule whose integral intersection $E_N=N\cap L_0\cap L_\infty$ satisfies $N\cong A\otimes_{\mathbb Z}E_N$. If a $\mathbb Z$-module $F$ maps to $M\cap(L_0+N)\cap(L_\infty+N)$, generates $M$ modulo $N$ over $A$, and maps injectively into $(L_0+\mathbb QN)/(qL_0+\mathbb QN)$ and $(L_\infty+\mathbb QN)/(q^{-1}L_\infty+\mathbb QN)$, then $M$ is balanced. The sequence
$$0\to(N\cap L_0)/(N\cap qL_0)\to(M\cap L_0)/(M\cap qL_0)\to(L_0+\mathbb QN)/(qL_0+\mathbb QN)$$
is exact, and its last image is the image of $F$. If $F$ and $E_N$ are finite free $\mathbb Z$-modules, then so is $E_M=M\cap L_0\cap L_\infty$, and $M$ is free over $A$.

These are the integral forms of Kashiwara's chart lemmas, in the notation of [[def-balanced-triple-and-globalization-map]]; their rational base extension gives the usual $A_0/A_\infty$ criterion, and no containment of charts or freeness of $M$ is assumed anywhere.

Let $i\in I$ and let $e_i'$ be the skew derivation of [[def-kashiwara-skew-derivations-on-the-negative-quantum-half]], with string decomposition $u=\sum_lF_i^{(l)}u_l$, $u_l\in\ker e_i'$ ([[thm-unique-kashiwara-i-string-decomposition]]).

(i) If $u\in U_A^-$ then all $u_l$ lie in $U_A^-$. The integral projector is
$$P_i=\sum_l(-1)^lq_i^{-l(l-1)/2}F_i^{(l)}(e_i')^l,\qquad u_l=q_i^{l(l-1)/2}P_i(e_i')^lu,$$
where all powers of $e_i'$ are ordinary powers, not divided by $[l]_i!$.

(ii) Define
$$I_{(i,n)}^A:=U_A^-\cap F_i^nU_q^-=\bigoplus_{l\ge n}F_i^{(l)}\bigl(\ker e_i'\cap U_A^-\bigr)=\sum_{l\ge n}F_i^{(l)}U_A^-,$$
$$J_{(i,n)}^A:=\pi_\lambda\bigl(I_{(i,n)}^A\bigr)=\sum_{l\ge n}F_i^{(l)}V_A(\lambda),$$
with $\pi_\lambda(P)=Pv_\lambda$ and $V_A(\lambda)=U_A^-v_\lambda$ as in [[def-integral-residue-lattices-of-the-negative-half-and-highest-weight-modules]]. The latter is an $A$-submodule inside the field string-image subspace $F_i^nV(\lambda)$, not a $U_q$-submodule or a $U_A$-stable lattice in general; its equality with $V_A(\lambda)\cap F_i^nV(\lambda)$ is proved after the adapted global basis construction, not presumed here.

(iii) The integral residue of $I_{(i,n)}^A\cap\mathcal L(\infty)$ is the free $\mathbb Z$-span of $\mathcal B(\infty)\cap\tilde f_i^n\mathcal B(\infty)$, and the corresponding rational residue of $F_i^nU_q^-\cap\mathcal L(\infty)$ is its $\mathbb Q$-span. Integral balancedness of the zero/infinity triple of $I_{(i,n)}^A$ is a conclusion of the subsequent string-ideal induction, not an input.

(iv) On every $U_A$-stable integrable module lattice $M_A$, if a label $\mu$ satisfies $\langle h_i,\mu\rangle=-n\le-1$, then every $u\in(M_A)_\mu$ satisfies the finite identity
$$u=\sum_{k\ge n}(-1)^{k-n}\binom{k-1}{k-n}_iF_i^{(k)}E_i^{(k)}u,$$
and consequently $(M_A)_\mu=\sum_{k\ge n}F_i^{(k)}(M_A)_{\mu+k\alpha_i}$. This is the exact boundary generation supplier used in the string-ideal induction.

Let $\star$ be the $\mathbb Q(q)$-linear anti-involution of $U_q^-$ fixing each generator $F_i$, so that for a word $F_{i_1}\cdots F_{i_r}$ one has $(F_{i_1}\cdots F_{i_r})^\star=F_{i_r}\cdots F_{i_1}$, and let $B$ be the normalized Kashiwara half form of [[thm-the-negative-half-bilinear-form-is-symmetric-nondegenerate-and-integral]]. Then $\star$ is a well-defined anti-involution of the Serre quotient, reverses negative words, preserves the divided-power integral form $U_A^-$ of [[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]], commutes with the bar involution $\psi$, and preserves $B$: $B(P^\star,Q^\star)=B(P,Q)$. Consequently $\star$ preserves the crystal lattice $\mathcal L(\infty)$ of [[lem-crystal-lattice-polarizations-are-perfect-at-q-zero]], the integral residue lattice $L_{\mathbb Z}(\infty)=U_A^-\cap\mathcal L(\infty)$, and the bar lattice $L_{\mathbb Z}^-=U_A^-\cap\psi(\mathcal L(\infty))$ of [[lem-integral-crystal-residues-of-the-negative-half-represent-the-crystal-basis]]. On the integral crystal residue the induced map permutes $\mathcal B(\infty)\cup(-\mathcal B(\infty))$. Only this signed lattice preservation is asserted, not an unsigned $\star$-crystal theorem; the sign is what the gluing of the string-ideal global lifts requires.

Let $\lambda\in P^+$ and let $V(\lambda)=L(\lambda)$ be the simple integrable highest weight module with highest weight vector $v_\lambda$ ([[thm-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module-exists-and-is-unique]]). Let $\mathcal L(\lambda),\mathcal B(\lambda),\mathcal L(\infty),\mathcal B(\infty)$ be the lattices and generating residue sets of [[def-kashiwara-lattices-lambda-and-infinity]], let $\tilde e_i,\tilde f_i$ be the Kashiwara operators, let $\pi_\lambda:U_q^-\to V(\lambda)$, $\pi_\lambda(P)=Pv_\lambda$, and let $\Phi_{\lambda,\mu},\Psi_{\lambda,\mu}$ be the tensor maps of [[lem-highest-weight-tensor-maps-and-their-adjunction]]. For $\alpha=\sum_in_i\alpha_i\in Q_+$ write $|\alpha|:=\sum_in_i$ and $Q_+(r):=\{\alpha\in Q_+:\ |\alpha|\le r\}$.

(i) For every integer $r\ge0$ the following interlocking statements are all true.

- A(r): $\tilde e_i\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}\subseteq\mathcal L(\lambda)$ for all $i\in I$ and $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$.
- B(r): $\tilde e_i\mathcal B(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}\subseteq\mathcal B(\lambda)\cup\{0\}$ for all $i$ and $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$.
- C(r): for all $i$, $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$, $b\in\mathcal B(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha+\alpha_i}$ and $b'\in\mathcal B(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$, one has $\tilde f_ib=b'$ if and only if $b=\tilde e_ib'$.
- D(r): for all $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$, $\mathcal B(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$ is a $\mathbb Q$-basis of $\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}/q\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$.
- E(r): for all $\lambda,\mu\in P^+$ and $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$, $\Phi_{\lambda,\mu}(\mathcal L(\lambda+\mu)_{\lambda+\mu-\alpha})\subseteq\mathcal L(\lambda)\otimes\mathcal L(\mu)$.
- F(r): for all $\lambda,\mu\in P^+$ and $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$, $\Psi_{\lambda,\mu}((\mathcal L(\lambda)\otimes\mathcal L(\mu))_{\lambda+\mu-\alpha})\subseteq\mathcal L(\lambda+\mu)$.
- G(r): $\Psi_{\lambda,\mu}((\mathcal B(\lambda)\otimes\mathcal B(\mu))_{\lambda+\mu-\alpha})\subseteq\mathcal B(\lambda+\mu)\cup\{0\}$ for all $\lambda,\mu$ and $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$.
- H(r): $\tilde e_i\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha}\subseteq\mathcal L(\infty)$ for all $i$ and $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$.
- I(r): $\tilde e_i\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\alpha}\subseteq\mathcal B(\infty)\cup\{0\}$ for all $i$ and $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$.
- J(r): for all $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$ and $b\in\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\alpha}$ with $\tilde e_ib\neq0$, one has $b=\tilde f_i\tilde e_ib$.
- K(r): $\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\alpha}$ is a $\mathbb Q$-basis of $\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha}/q\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha}$ for all $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$.
- L(r): $\pi_\lambda(\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha})=\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$ for all $\lambda\in P^+$ and $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$.
- M(r): for all $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$, $i\in I$, $\lambda\in P^+$ and $P\in\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha+\alpha_i}$, one has $\tilde f_i(Pv_\lambda)\equiv(\tilde f_iP)v_\lambda\bmod q\mathcal L(\lambda)$.
- N(r): for all $\lambda\in P^+$ and $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$, $\pi_\lambda$ induces a bijection $\{b\in\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\alpha}:\pi_\lambda(b)\neq0\}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal B(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$.
- O(r): for all $\lambda\in P^+$, $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$ and $b\in\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\alpha}$ with $\pi_\lambda(b)\neq0$, one has $\pi_\lambda(\tilde e_ib)=\tilde e_i\pi_\lambda(b)$.

(ii) Consequently $(\mathcal L(\lambda),\mathcal B(\lambda))$ is a crystal basis of $V(\lambda)$ in the sense of [[def-crystal-lattice-and-crystal-basis]]: $\mathcal L(\lambda)$ is a crystal lattice of $V(\lambda)$, $\mathcal B(\lambda)$ is a $\mathbb Q$-basis of $\mathcal L(\lambda)/q\mathcal L(\lambda)$ with $\mathcal B(\lambda)=\bigsqcup_\mu\mathcal B(\lambda)_\mu$, the operators satisfy $\tilde e_i\mathcal B(\lambda)\subseteq\mathcal B(\lambda)\cup\{0\}$ and the partial-inverse axiom, and $\dim_{\mathbb Q(q)}V(\lambda)_\mu=\#\mathcal B(\lambda)_\mu$ for all $\mu$. The lattices $\mathcal L(\lambda)_\mu$ and $\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha}$ are free $A_0$-modules.

Let $\mathcal L(\infty)\subseteq U_q^-$ and $\mathcal B(\infty)\subseteq\mathcal L(\infty)/q\mathcal L(\infty)$ be the Kashiwara lattice and generating set of [[def-kashiwara-lattices-lambda-and-infinity]], with the Kashiwara operators $\tilde e_i,\tilde f_i$ on $U_q^-$ of [[thm-the-i-string-decomposition-of-the-negative-half]](iii).

(i) $(\mathcal L(\infty),\mathcal B(\infty))$ is a crystal basis of $U_q^-$ in the sense of [[def-crystal-lattice-and-crystal-basis]]: $\mathcal L(\infty)$ is a free $A_0$-submodule with $U_q^-\cong\mathbb Q(q)\otimes_{A_0}\mathcal L(\infty)$, stable under $\tilde e_i$ and $\tilde f_i$; and $\mathcal B(\infty)$ is a $\mathbb Q$-basis of $\mathcal L(\infty)/q\mathcal L(\infty)$ satisfying $\tilde e_i\mathcal B(\infty)\subseteq\mathcal B(\infty)\cup\{0\}$, $\tilde f_i\mathcal B(\infty)\subseteq\mathcal B(\infty)$, and $\tilde f_ib=b'$ if and only if $b=\tilde e_ib'$ for all $b,b'\in\mathcal B(\infty)$.

(ii) The root-graded components are free: $\mathcal L(\infty)=\bigoplus_{\nu\in Q_+}\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\nu}$ and each $\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\nu}$ is a free $A_0$-module of rank $\#\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\nu}=\dim_{\mathbb Q(q)}U_q^-[-\nu]$.

(iii) For every $\lambda\in P^+$ the projection $\pi_\lambda(P)=Pv_\lambda$ maps $\mathcal B(\infty)$ onto $\mathcal B(\lambda)\cup\{0\}$, and the compatibility statements of [[lem-crystal-operators-commute-with-highest-weight-projection-modulo-q]] hold: $\pi_\lambda(\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha})=\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$, $\{b\in\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\alpha}:\pi_\lambda(b)\neq0\}\cong\mathcal B(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$, $\tilde f_i\pi_\lambda=\pi_\lambda\tilde f_i$ and $\tilde e_i\pi_\lambda(b)=\pi_\lambda(\tilde e_ib)$ whenever $\pi_\lambda(b)\neq0$.

(iv) The root-graded crystal has finite $\varepsilon_i$ on each element, formal $\varphi_i=\varepsilon_i+\langle h_i,\mathrm{wt}\rangle$, and actual lowering length $\ell_i^-=\infty$. Every $\tilde f_i$-iterate is nonzero because $\tilde e_i\tilde f_i=\mathrm{id}$ holds on its lattice and residue. Thus it is the infinite lowering crystal of the unit, with the negative-half convention of the crystal-graph definition.

**Choice.** The axiom of choice is declared via [[def-axiom-of-choice]] and enters only through the grand loop: the partial-inverse axiom in (i) uses clause J(r) of [[thm-grand-loop-existence-of-highest-weight-crystal-bases]], whose proof consumes the AC-dependent form comparison of the negative-half form. The freeness and rank statements are choice-free.

Let $\lambda\in P^+$ and let $\mathcal L(\lambda),\mathcal B(\lambda),\mathcal L(\infty),\mathcal B(\infty)$ be the lattices and bases of [[def-kashiwara-lattices-lambda-and-infinity]], with $\pi_\lambda:U_q^-\to V(\lambda)$, $P\mapsto Pv_\lambda$, and Kashiwara operators $\tilde e_i,\tilde f_i$. Then for every $\alpha\in Q_+$, every $i\in I$ and every $\lambda\in P^+$:

(a) **Lattice projection.** $\pi_\lambda(\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha})=\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$.

(b) **Operator compatibility modulo $q$.** For every $P\in\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha+\alpha_i}$, $\tilde f_i(Pv_\lambda)\equiv(\tilde f_iP)v_\lambda\bmod q\mathcal L(\lambda)$, and for every $b\in\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\alpha}$ with $\pi_\lambda(b)\neq0$, $\tilde e_i\pi_\lambda(b)=\pi_\lambda(\tilde e_ib)$ in $\mathcal L(\lambda)/q\mathcal L(\lambda)$. Equivalently $\tilde f_i\pi_\lambda=\pi_\lambda\tilde f_i$ on $\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\alpha+\alpha_i}$, where the left-hand side is computed in $V(\lambda)$.

(c) **Basis projection.** The map induced by $\pi_\lambda$ is a bijection $\{b\in\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\alpha}:\pi_\lambda(b)\neq0\}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal B(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$.

(d) **Large-weight form.** If all $\lambda(h_j)$, $j\in I$, are sufficiently large compared with $\alpha$, then $\pi_\lambda$ induces isomorphisms $\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$ and $\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\alpha}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal B(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$, and the congruences of (b) for such $\lambda$ are the computation used inside the grand loop to deduce the general case; the general statements (a)-(c) hold for every $\lambda\in P^+$, without a largeness hypothesis.

**Choice.** The axiom of choice is declared via [[def-axiom-of-choice]]: clause (c) is clause N(r) of [[thm-grand-loop-existence-of-highest-weight-crystal-bases]], whose proof applies clause J(r), and J(r) is where the AC-dependent form comparison of [[thm-the-negative-half-bilinear-form-is-symmetric-nondegenerate-and-integral]] is used. Clauses (a), (b) and (d) are themselves choice-free.

Let $\lambda\in P^+$ and let $L(\lambda)$ be the simple integrable highest weight module with highest weight vector $v_\lambda$ ([[thm-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module-exists-and-is-unique]]); in this page we write $V(\lambda):=L(\lambda)$, following the notation of the crystal sources. Let $U_q^-$ be the negative half with its Kashiwara operators $\tilde e_i,\tilde f_i$ ([[thm-the-i-string-decomposition-of-the-negative-half]]), and let $A_0$ be the crystal limiting ring ([[def-the-local-ring-at-q-zero]]).

Define $\mathcal L(\lambda)$ to be the $A_0$-submodule of $V(\lambda)$ generated by all vectors $\tilde f_{i_1}\cdots\tilde f_{i_r}v_\lambda$ ($r\ge0$, $i_1,\dots,i_r\in I$), where for $r=0$ the vector is $v_\lambda$; and $\mathcal L(\infty)$ to be the $A_0$-submodule of $U_q^-$ generated by all $\tilde f_{i_1}\cdots\tilde f_{i_r}\mathbf 1$ ($r\ge0$), where $\mathbf 1$ is the unit of $U_q^-$. Here $\tilde f_i$ on $V(\lambda)$ are the module Kashiwara operators and $\tilde f_i$ on $U_q^-$ are the negative-half operators. Define
$$\mathcal B(\lambda):=\{\tilde f_{i_1}\cdots\tilde f_{i_r}v_\lambda+q\mathcal L(\lambda):r\ge0\}\setminus\{0\}\subseteq\mathcal L(\lambda)/q\mathcal L(\lambda),$$
$$\mathcal B(\infty):=\{\tilde f_{i_1}\cdots\tilde f_{i_r}\mathbf 1+q\mathcal L(\infty):r\ge0\}\setminus\{0\}\subseteq\mathcal L(\infty)/q\mathcal L(\infty).$$

Then, with $\pi_\lambda:U_q^-\to V(\lambda)$, $\pi_\lambda(P)=Pv_\lambda$:

(a) $\mathcal L(\lambda)=\bigoplus_{\mu\in P}\mathcal L(\lambda)_\mu$ with $\mathcal L(\lambda)_\mu=\mathcal L(\lambda)\cap V(\lambda)_\mu$, and $\mathcal L(\infty)=\bigoplus_{\nu\in Q_+}\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\nu}$ with $\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\nu}=\mathcal L(\infty)\cap U_q^-[-\nu]$; correspondingly $\mathcal B(\lambda)=\bigsqcup_\mu\mathcal B(\lambda)_\mu$ and $\mathcal B(\infty)=\bigsqcup_\nu\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\nu}$.

(b) $\tilde f_i\mathcal L(\lambda)\subseteq\mathcal L(\lambda)$ and $\tilde f_i\mathcal L(\infty)\subseteq\mathcal L(\infty)$.

(c) (Recursive spanning.) For $\alpha\in Q_+\setminus\{0\}$,
$$\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}=\sum_{i\in I}\tilde f_i\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha+\alpha_i},\qquad \mathcal B(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}=\Bigl(\bigcup_{i\in I}\tilde f_i\mathcal B(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha+\alpha_i}\Bigr)\setminus\{0\},$$
and the same formulas with $\mathcal L(\infty),\mathcal B(\infty)$. Each $\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$ and each $\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha}$ is generated over $A_0$ by finitely many monomials of total length at most $\operatorname{ht}(\alpha)$, hence is a finitely generated $A_0$-module.

No basis property, scalar-extension spanning or crystal-lattice property of $\mathcal L(\lambda)$ or $\mathcal L(\infty)$ is asserted here; these are conclusions of the grand loop. The script letters avoid the collision with the simple module $L(\lambda)$. No choice principle is used. Each fixed component is torsionfree inside a field vector space and generated by finitely many words of its fixed height, so it is free over the DVR $A_0$; its full field-span is proved later. The field map $\pi_\lambda$ is surjective, but exact equality on Kashiwara monomial generators is not asserted.

Let $L_{\mathbb Z}(\infty)=U_A^-\cap\mathcal L(\infty)$ be the integral residue lattice of [[def-integral-residue-lattices-of-the-negative-half-and-highest-weight-modules]], with $L_{\mathbb Z}/qL_{\mathbb Z}\to\mathcal L(\infty)/q\mathcal L(\infty)$ the canonical injection. Then the image of this injection is exactly $\bigoplus_{b\in\mathcal B(\infty)}\mathbb Z b$; in particular $L_{\mathbb Z}/qL_{\mathbb Z}$ is a free $\mathbb Z$-module with basis $\mathcal B(\infty)$, and after tensoring with $\mathbb Q$ it is the full rational crystal space $\mathbb Q\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\bigoplus_b\mathbb Zb=\mathcal L(\infty)/q\mathcal L(\infty)$.

The normalized Kashiwara half form of [[thm-the-negative-half-bilinear-form-is-symmetric-nondegenerate-and-integral]] takes values on $U_A^-$ in $K_{\mathbb Z}=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1},(1-q^{2n})^{-1}:n\ge1]$ and on $L_{\mathbb Z}$ in $A_{\mathbb Z}=\mathbb Z[q,(1-q^{2n})^{-1}:n\ge1]$; consequently its residue pairing on $L_{\mathbb Z}/qL_{\mathbb Z}$ is $\mathbb Z$-valued. In the residue basis $\mathcal B(\infty)$ the coefficients of an integral element are its integer pairings with the basis vectors, and the elements of $L_{\mathbb Z}$ of norm $1$ are exactly $\mathcal B(\infty)\cup(-\mathcal B(\infty))$. The Kashiwara operators $\tilde e_i,\tilde f_i$ preserve $L_{\mathbb Z}$, hence induce endomorphisms of the integral residue subgroup. No $A$-module structure on $L_{\mathbb Z}$, no identification of the integral residue with the rational residue as a $\mathbb Z$-module, and no unsigned norm-$1$ characterization is asserted; the module integral residue basis is established only in the globalization theorem of this page.

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum with $a_{ii}=2$ for
all $i$ ([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]) and let $M$ be a
$P$-graded type-one quantum weight module
([[def-quantum-weight-module-and-integrability]]) whose support is contained in
a finite union of cones,

$$\operatorname{supp}M\subseteq\bigcup_{j=1}^{s}(\lambda_j-Q_+)\qquad(\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_s\in P),$$

where $Q_+=\bigoplus_i\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\alpha_i$. Choose a finite free direct
coordinate summand $X_f\subseteq P$ (with respect to a free basis of $P$,
[[def-free-abelian-group]]) containing all $\lambda_j$ and all $\alpha_i$, and
set

$$Y_{\mathrm{aux}}:=\Bigl(\bigoplus_{i\in I}\mathbb ZH_i\Bigr)\oplus\operatorname{Hom}(X_f,\mathbb Z),\qquad X_{\mathrm{aux}}:=\operatorname{Hom}(Y_{\mathrm{aux}},\mathbb Z),$$

with the evaluation pairing $X_{\mathrm{aux}}\times Y_{\mathrm{aux}}\to\mathbb Z$.
Define $j\colon X_f\to X_{\mathrm{aux}}$ by $j(x)(H_i):=\langle x,h_i\rangle$ and
$j(x)(f):=f(x)$ for $f\in\operatorname{Hom}(X_f,\mathbb Z)$, and put
$\alpha_i^{\mathrm{aux}}:=j(\alpha_i)$. Then:

(i) $(I,A,D,X_{\mathrm{aux}},Y_{\mathrm{aux}},q)$ with the simple roots
$\alpha_i^{\mathrm{aux}}$ and simple coroots $H_i$ is a symmetrizable Cartan
datum for a quantum group with the same generalized Cartan matrix $A$ and the
same symmetrizer $D$; its pairing is perfect, the $\alpha_i^{\mathrm{aux}}$ are
linearly independent, the $H_i$ are primitive and independent, and integral
fundamental weights $\Lambda_j$ ($\Lambda_j(H_i)=\delta_{ij}$) exist. Here
$\langle\alpha_j^{\mathrm{aux}},H_i\rangle=a_{ij}$ is the original convention
([[def-realization-of-a-generalized-cartan-matrix]],
[[prop-minimal-realizations-exist-and-are-unique-up-to-isomorphism]]).

(ii) $M$ carries a unique structure of $X_{\mathrm{aux}}$-graded type-one
quantum weight module for the auxiliary datum with
$\operatorname{supp}M^{\mathrm{aux}}\subseteq j(X_f)$, namely
$$M^{\mathrm{aux}}_{j(x)}:=M_x\quad(x\in X_f),\qquad M^{\mathrm{aux}}_{\xi}:=0\quad(\xi\notin j(X_f)),$$
$$K_{(n,f)}\ \text{acts on}\ M_x\ \text{by}\ q^{\sum_in_i\langle x,h_i\rangle+f(x)}\qquad\bigl((n,f)\in\textstyle\bigoplus_i\mathbb ZH_i\oplus\operatorname{Hom}(X_f,\mathbb Z)\bigr),$$
with the actions of $E_i$, $F_i$ and of the simple coroots
$K_{d_iH_i}$ unchanged. In particular the old $K_h$ action is recovered from
the label $x$ as $q^{\langle x,h\rangle}$, and the old and auxiliary $E_i,F_i$
actions agree.

(iii) The two recipes are inverse on objects and grading-preserving morphisms:
on $U_q(\mathfrak g)$-modules with labels in $X_f$ and support as above, the
identity on underlying vector spaces is an equivalence between the category of
$P$-graded type-one modules and the corresponding full subcategory of
$X_{\mathrm{aux}}$-graded type-one modules with labels in $j(X_f)$. This is not
an embedding of the old torus algebra into the new one and is asserted only
inside this finite-support category.

(iv) The construction applies simultaneously to Verma modules and highest weight
modules (supported in $\lambda-Q_+$) and to finite tensor products of such
modules (labels add), by choosing one $X_f$ containing all participating upper
weights and all simple roots; the comultiplication's $E_i,F_i$ formulas are
unchanged because only the diagonal toral characters change.

(v) Rationally, $h_{\mathrm{aux}}:=Y_{\mathrm{aux}}\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\mathbb Q$
decomposes as $h_{\mathrm{aux}}=H_{\min}\oplus Z$, where $H_{\min}$ is a
minimal realization of $A$ (of dimension $2n-r$, $n=|I|$, $r=\operatorname{rank}A$)
and $Z\subseteq\ker\alpha$ is a complement on which all $\alpha_i^{\mathrm{aux}}$
vanish, so the elements of $Z$ are central in the correspondingly extended
Kac–Moody algebra; hence the classical Cartan and multiplicity comparisons of
[[prop-minimal-realizations-exist-and-are-unique-up-to-isomorphism]] apply to
$H_{\min}$.

Let $\lambda\in P$ be a dominant integral label weight, put
$m_i:=\langle\lambda,h_i\rangle\ge0$, and let $M(\lambda)$ be the quantum Verma
module with highest vector $v_\lambda$
([[def-quantum-verma-module-and-simple-highest-weight-quotient]],
[[def-kac-moody-integral-and-dominant-integral-weights]]).

(i) The quotient $\tilde L(\lambda):=M(\lambda)/\sum_iU_q(\mathfrak g)F_i^{(m_i+1)}v_\lambda$
is nonzero, has finite-dimensional label weights and support
$\lambda-Q_+$, is integrable, and equals the canonical simple highest weight
module $L(\lambda)$, which is simple also as an ordinary (not assumed graded)
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module.

(ii) **Universality.** Every integrable cyclic highest weight module $V$ of
highest weight $\lambda$ with highest vector $v\ne0$ receives a
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module map $\tilde L(\lambda)\to V$ with
$\bar v_\lambda\mapsto v$, and this map is unique; every nonzero such $V$ is
isomorphic to $L(\lambda)$.

(iii) Its character equals the classical integrable highest weight character of
the explicitly regularized realization of the datum. No global
$\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-freeness and no crystal or global basis is used.

Let $\lambda\in P$ be dominant integral, so $m_i:=\langle\lambda,h_i\rangle\ge0$
for all $i$, and let $M(\lambda)$ be the Verma module with highest vector
$v_\lambda$ ([[def-quantum-verma-module-and-simple-highest-weight-quotient]]).
Put $s_i:=F_i^{(m_i+1)}v_\lambda$.

(i) Every $s_i$ is a singular (highest weight) vector of weight
$\lambda-(m_i+1)\alpha_i$.

(ii) The graded submodule
$S:=\sum_iU_q(\mathfrak g)s_i=\sum_iU_q^-s_i$ is proper, and the quotient
$\tilde L(\lambda):=M(\lambda)/S$ is nonzero, has finite-dimensional
label-weight spaces, and is integrable ([[def-quantum-weight-module-and-integrability]]).

(iii) Every integrable cyclic highest weight module $V$ of highest weight
$\lambda$ is a quotient of $\tilde L(\lambda)$.

No commutation between divided powers $F_i^{(a)},F_j^{(b)}$ of distinct indices
with $a_{ij}\ne0$ is assumed anywhere.

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum for a quantum
group with $a_{ii}=2$ for all $i$
([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]), let
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be its Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra
([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]) with $q_i=q^{d_i}$ and
$K_i=K_{d_ih_i}$, and set

$$A:=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]\ \subseteq\ \mathbb Q(q),$$

the image of the Laurent polynomial ring $\Lambda_1=\mathbb Z[t]_{S}$ of
[[def-the-laurent-polynomial-ring]] under the unital ring homomorphism sending
$t$ to the indeterminate $q$; this homomorphism is injective and $A$ is a
subring of $\mathbb Q(q)$ (Verification, step 1.1). We work over this
commutative domain $A$ inside the field $\mathbb Q(q)$.

For $i\in I$, $c\in\mathbb Z$ and $t\ge0$ define the **toral quantum binomial**

$$T_{i,c,t}:=\begin{bmatrix}K_i;c\\ t\end{bmatrix}:=\prod_{s=1}^{t}\frac{K_iq_i^{\,c-s+1}-K_i^{-1}q_i^{\,-c+s-1}}{q_i^{\,s}-q_i^{\,-s}}\in U_q(\mathfrak g),$$

the empty product being $T_{i,c,0}:=1$. Each factor is defined in
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$ because $q_i^{\,s}-q_i^{\,-s}\ne0$ for $s\ge1$
([[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]), so
$T_{i,c,t}$ is a polynomial in $K_i^{\pm1}$ with coefficients in $\mathbb Q(q)$;
in particular all $T_{i,c,t}$ commute with the $K_h$ and with one another
(Verification, step 2.1).

The **Lusztig divided-power integral form** is the $A$-subalgebra

$$U_A:=\bigl\langle E_i^{(r)},\ F_i^{(r)},\ K_h^{\pm1},\ T_{i,c,t}\ \colon\ i\in I,\ r,t\ge0,\ c\in\mathbb Z,\ h\in P^{\vee}\bigr\rangle\ \subseteq\ U_q(\mathfrak g),$$

where $x^{(r)}=x^r/[r]_i!$ are the divided powers of
[[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]. Write $U_A^\pm$
for the $A$-subalgebras generated by the $E_i^{(r)}$ and by the $F_i^{(r)}$,
and $U_A^0$ for the one generated by the $K_h^{\pm1}$ and the $T_{i,c,t}$.

Then:

(i) $U_A$ contains $E_i=E_i^{(1)}$, $F_i=F_i^{(1)}$ and all $K_h$;

(ii) $U_A$ is a root-graded $A$-subalgebra of the root-graded
$\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ ([[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]):
with $U_A[\beta]:=U_A\cap U_q(\mathfrak g)[\beta]$ one has
$U_A=\bigoplus_{\beta\in Q}U_A[\beta]$, each $U_A[\beta]$ is an $A$-submodule,
and $U_A^\pm,U_A^0$ are graded in the same way;

(iii) $U_A\otimes_A\mathbb Q(q)\cong U_q(\mathfrak g)$ canonically, i.e. the
$\mathbb Q(q)$-span of $U_A$ is all of $U_q(\mathfrak g)$.

The shifted binomials $T_{i,c,t}$ with $c\ne0$ are included because the
divided-power reordering identity of
[[lem-divided-power-and-toral-quantum-binomial-reordering-identities]] has
coefficients $T_{i,2t-a-b,t}$ with a nonconstant index; the specializations at
$q=1$ of these elements are computed in
[[lem-q-one-toral-specialization-identifies-the-classical-cartan-generators]],
and the integral triangular decomposition and the specialization are treated
only after this definition.

No freeness of $U_A$ or of its parts over $A$, no independence of the listed
generators, and no triangularity of the products of the three parts is asserted
here. In particular $A$ is not a principal ideal domain (Verification, step
7.1), so no torsion-free-to-free inference over $A$ is permitted anywhere on
this page.

Let $R=\mathbb C\llbracket\hbar\rrbracket$, $K=\mathbb C((\hbar))$, $q=e^\hbar$, and $q_i=e^{d_i\hbar}$ for a finite symmetrizable Cartan datum. Let $H^+=U_\hbar\mathfrak n^+$, $\langle V\rangle$ and the shuffle product be as in [[def-formal-quantum-shuffle-borel-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]], and put $H^-=T(V^*)/J_-$ using [[lem-quantum-serre-sums-vanish-in-the-formal-quantum-shuffle-algebra]]. Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]), used only through the formal embedding theorem. For an indeterminate $z$, let $H_z^\pm$ be the algebras over $\mathbb C(z)$ presented by the separate symmetric quantum Serre relations, with parameters $z_i=z^{d_i}$.

(i) Each $H^\pm[\pm\alpha]$ is finite free over $R$, and
$$\operatorname{rank}_R H^\pm[\pm\alpha]=\dim_{\mathbb C}U(\mathfrak n^\pm)[\pm\alpha]=\dim_{\mathbb C(z)}H_z^\pm[\pm\alpha].$$
Every family of homogeneous lifts of a basis of the classical component is an $R$-basis. Likewise, homogeneous word expressions with coefficients rational in $z$, regular at $z=1$, which reduce to a classical component basis form a basis of the corresponding generic component. In particular, for a supplied ordered homogeneous basis of $\mathfrak n^\pm$, ordered monomials in any such regular lifts form a generic PBW basis.

(ii) Both formal halves are graded braided Hopf algebras. Their generators are primitive, their counits kill positive height, and their tensor squares use
$$ (u\otimes v)(u'\otimes v')=q^{-\langle\deg u',\deg v\rangle}uu'\otimes vv',\qquad \langle\epsilon_i,\epsilon_j\rangle=d_i a_{ij},$$
with negative degrees for $H^-$. The word pairing restricts and descends to a nondegenerate $K$-valued pairing $H^+\times H^-$ with $\langle e_i,f_j\rangle=\delta_{ij}/(\hbar d_i)$ and $\langle1,1\rangle=1$. It is zero on unequal opposite degrees and satisfies the braided Hopf adjunctions
$$\langle x,yy'\rangle=\sum\langle x_{(1)},y\rangle\langle x_{(2)},y'\rangle,\qquad\langle xx',y\rangle=\sum\langle x,y_{(1)}\rangle\langle x',y_{(2)}\rangle.$$
The generic halves have the same braided Hopf structures and a nondegenerate $\mathbb C(z)$-valued pairing normalized by $\langle e_i,f_j\rangle_z=\delta_{ij}/(z_i-z_i^{-1})$. Thus opposite graded components are dual. All generic assertions also hold for the corresponding $\mathbb Q(z)$-presentations and their rational pairing, with the PBW lift clause using bases of the rational classical Serre form.

derivations.claim: **Simultaneous induction and the base layer.** Replace the assertions by the following height-$r$ induction statements: X$(r)$: the triple of $U_A^-$ is integrally balanced in every degree of height $\le r$ with bar-invariant global lifts $G_\infty(b)$ forming an $A$-basis and $\mathbb Z$-intersection $\mathbb Z\mathcal B(\infty)$; Y$(r)$: the same for every $V_A(\lambda)$ with lifts $G_\lambda(b)$ and intersection $\mathbb Z\mathcal B(\lambda)$; Z$(r)$: the negative-half membership $G_\infty(b)\in I_{(i,1)}^A$ whenever $\tilde e_ib\ne0$, for every new degree of height $\le r$; and the derived clause D$(r)$: for the new degrees, the based-quotient compatibility $\pi_\lambda(G_\infty(b))=0$ if and only if $\pi_\lambda(b)=0$, and $\pi_\lambda(G_\infty(b))=G_\lambda(\pi_\lambda(b))$ otherwise. For $r=0$ the degree component is $A\cdot1$ or $Av_\lambda$, the charts meet in $\mathbb Z\cdot1$ or $\mathbb Z v_\lambda$, and the stated properties hold by inspection. Assume X, Y, Z, D for all heights $<r$ and fix a degree $\alpha$ of height $r\ge1$.

**The string ideals at height $r$ are balanced.** The induction hypotheses are exactly the input of [F1] at height $r$, so for every $i\in I$ and $n\ge1$ the ideals $I_{(i,n)}^A$ and $J_{(i,n)}^A$ are integrally balanced in degree $-\alpha$, respectively $\lambda-\alpha$, with adapted free bases whose balanced $\mathbb Z$-intersections map isomorphically onto $\mathbb Z(\mathcal B(\infty)\cap\tilde f_i^n\mathcal B(\infty))$ and $\mathbb Z(\mathcal B(\lambda)\cap\tilde f_i^n\mathcal B(\lambda))$. In particular, for each $b\in\mathcal B(\infty)\cap\tilde f_i^n\mathcal B(\infty)$ there is an adapted lift $g\in E_{I_{(i,n)}}:=I_{(i,n)}^A\cap\mathcal L(\infty)\cap\psi(\mathcal L(\infty))$ whose residue class in $(I_{(i,n)}^A\cap\mathcal L(\infty))/(I_{(i,n)}^A\cap q\mathcal L(\infty))$ is $b$; these are the only lifts used below.

**Every string lift is bar fixed.** Let $g\in E_I:=I_{(i,n)}^A\cap\mathcal L(\infty)\cap\psi(\mathcal L(\infty))$ be any adapted lift. By [F3] the ideal $I_{(i,n)}^A$ is generated over $A$ by bar-fixed divided-word vectors, so write $g=\sum_wa_ww$ with $a_w\in A$ and $\psi(w)=w$; then $g-\psi(g)=\sum_w(a_w-\psi(a_w))w$, and each antisymmetric Laurent polynomial $a_w-\psi(a_w)$ is divisible in $A$ by $q-q^{-1}$, so $h:=\bigl(g-\psi(g)\bigr)/(q-q^{-1})\in I_{(i,n)}^A$. Since $g,\psi(g)\in\mathcal L(\infty)\cap\psi(\mathcal L(\infty))$ and $(q-q^{-1})^{-1}=-q(1-q^2)^{-1}\in qA_0$, one gets $h\in q\mathcal L(\infty)$; since $(q-q^{-1})^{-1}=q^{-1}(1-q^{-2})^{-1}\in A_\infty$, one gets $h\in\psi(\mathcal L(\infty))$. Thus $h\in E_I$ and $h\in q\mathcal L(\infty)$, so its class in $(I_{(i,n)}^A\cap\mathcal L(\infty))/(I_{(i,n)}^A\cap q\mathcal L(\infty))\cong\mathbb Z(\mathcal B(\infty)\cap\tilde f_i^n\mathcal B(\infty))$ is zero; by injectivity of the balanced residue map of [F2](1) applied to $I_{(i,n)}^A$, $h=0$ and $g=\psi(g)$. The same argument applies to the module ideals $J_{(i,n)}^A$.

**Gluing across colors (Kashiwara’s gluing lemma).** Let $b\in\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\alpha}$ lie in $\tilde f_i\mathcal B(\infty)\cap\tilde f_j\mathcal B(\infty)$, and let $G_i(b),G_j(b)\in\mathcal L(\infty)\cap\psi(\mathcal L(\infty))$ be the corresponding adapted lifts of $I_{(i,1)}^A$ and $I_{(j,1)}^A$ from step 2.1. Write $b$ as a lowering word with rightmost color $k$ and choose, using [F7], a dominant integral auxiliary label $\lambda$ in the regular datum with $\lambda(h_k)=0$ and all other coordinates larger than the degree bounds. By the kernel statement of [F7], $\ker\pi_\lambda$ in degree $\alpha$ equals the image of $U_q^-F_k$, and $bv_\lambda=0$ because the word ends in the color $k$ of length $0$ at $v_\lambda$. For each of the two lifts, $G_i(b)v_\lambda$ lies in $J_{(i,1)}^A$ by [F3], lies in $q\mathcal L(\lambda)$ because its crystal residue $\pi_\lambda(b)=0$, and lies in $\psi(\mathcal L(\lambda))$ by bar invariance; the balancedness of $J_{(i,1)}^A$ from step 2.1 forces $G_i(b)v_\lambda=0$, and likewise $G_j(b)v_\lambda=0$. Hence $Q:=G_i(b)-G_j(b)$ lies in $U_A^-\cap U_q^-F_k$, in $q\mathcal L(\infty)$ (both lifts have residue $b$), and in $\psi(\mathcal L(\infty))$. By the reversal [F4], $Q^\star$ lies in $U_A^-\cap F_kU_q^-\cap q\mathcal L(\infty)\cap\psi(\mathcal L(\infty))$; by [F3], $U_A^-\cap F_kU_q^-=I_{(k,1)}^A$; and then the balancedness of $I_{(k,1)}^A$ from step 2.1 again forces $Q^\star=0$, hence $Q=0$.

**Global half lifts and spanning.** For $\alpha\ne0$, [F5] supplies for every $b\in\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\alpha}$ a color $i$ and a predecessor $b'\in\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\alpha+\alpha_i}$ with $b=\tilde f_ib'$, so $b\in\mathcal B(\infty)\cap\tilde f_i\mathcal B(\infty)$ and step 2.1 provides an adapted lift in $I_{(i,1)}^A$; define $G_\infty(b)$ to be this element. Step 3.2 shows the definition does not depend on the chosen color, and two lifts for the same color differ by an element of $E_I\cap q\mathcal L(\infty)=0$ by step 3.1, so $G_\infty(b)$ is well defined and bar invariant. By [F3], every divided-word generator in degree $-\alpha$ is divisible on the right by some $F_i$, hence $U_A^-=\sum_{i\in I}I_{(i,1)}^A$ in this degree; by step 2.1 and the lower-height part of the induction, each $I_{(i,1)}^A$ has the free $A$-basis $\{G_\infty(b):b\in\mathcal B(\infty)\cap\tilde f_i\mathcal B(\infty)\}$. Therefore $U_A^-$ in degree $-\alpha$ equals $\sum_{b\in\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\alpha}}AG_\infty(b)$, and X$(<r)$ supplies the lower-height components, so the family $(G_\infty(b))_b$ spans $U_A^-$ over $A$ in every degree of height $\le r$.

**The half triple is integrally balanced (X$(r)$).** Put $F:=\bigoplus_{b\in\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\alpha}}\mathbb ZG_\infty(b)$; it is a finite free $\mathbb Z$-module contained in $U_A^-\cap\mathcal L(\infty)\cap\psi(\mathcal L(\infty))$ because the lifts are bar invariant and lie in the adapted integers of the string ideals. It generates $U_A^-$ over $A$ by step 4.1. Its image in $\mathcal L(\infty)/q\mathcal L(\infty)$ is $\bigoplus_b\mathbb Zb$ by [F6], and its image under $\psi$ is another free $\mathbb Z$-span of the same rank inside the infinity residue; the two images are injective. Applying the chart generation criterion [F2](2) to $M=U_A^-$, $L_0=\mathcal L(\infty)$ and $L_\infty=\psi(\mathcal L(\infty))$ gives that the half triple in degree $-\alpha$ is integrally balanced, with $E=F$ and $E\to(U_A^-\cap\mathcal L(\infty))/(U_A^-\cap q\mathcal L(\infty))$ an isomorphism onto $\bigoplus_b\mathbb Zb$; the same holds in every lower degree by X$(<r)$, so X$(r)$ holds.

**String-ideal membership and the top-string transition (Z$(r)$).** Since each $G_\infty(b)$ with $b\in\tilde f_i^n\mathcal B(\infty)$ lies in $I_{(i,n)}^A$ by construction and the adapted basis of $I_{(i,n)}^A$ is free, step 2.1 and the injectivity of the balanced residue map identify $I_{(i,n)}^A=\bigoplus_{b\in\mathcal B(\infty)\cap\tilde f_i^n\mathcal B(\infty)}AG_\infty(b)$ in degree $-\alpha$; in particular $G_\infty(b)\in I_{(i,1)}^A$ whenever $\tilde e_ib\ne0$, proving Z$(r)$. Moreover, if $\tilde e_ib=0$ and $n\ge1$, then $F_i^{(n)}G_\infty(b)$ lies in $I_{(i,n)}^A$ with residue $\tilde f_i^nb$ in $I_{(i,n)}^A\cap\mathcal L(\infty)/q(\cdots)$; after subtracting from it the adapted lift $G_\infty(\tilde f_i^nb)\in E_{I_{(i,n)}}$, the difference lies in $E_{I_{(i,n)}}\cap q\mathcal L(\infty)=0$, since the two elements reduce to the same crystal class. Hence $G_\infty(\tilde f_i^nb)-F_i^{(n)}G_\infty(b)\in I_{(i,n+1)}^A$ exactly.

**Killed module images vanish.** Fix $\lambda\in P^+$ and let $b\in\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\alpha}$ have $\pi_\lambda(b)=0$. By [F5] choose $i$ with $\tilde e_ib\ne0$; then $b\in\tilde f_i\mathcal B(\infty)$, so $G_\infty(b)\in I_{(i,1)}^A$ by Z$(r)$ and $G_\infty(b)v_\lambda\in J_{(i,1)}^A$ by [F3]. Since its residue $\pi_\lambda(b)$ is zero it lies in $q\mathcal L(\lambda)$, and since $G_\infty(b)$ is bar invariant and $\pi_\lambda$ commutes with $\psi$ it lies in $\psi(\mathcal L(\lambda))$. The balancedness of $J_{(i,1)}^A$ from step 2.1 forces the class of $G_\infty(b)v_\lambda$ in its balanced intersection to be zero, so $G_\infty(b)v_\lambda=0$; this is the local form of Kashiwara’s killed-image lemma.

**The surviving module images.** For $\pi_\lambda(b)\ne0$, the element $G_\infty(b)v_\lambda$ is bar invariant, lies in $\mathcal L(\lambda)$ by the lattice projection of [F5], and its residue in $\mathcal L(\lambda)/q\mathcal L(\lambda)$ is $\pi_\lambda(b)$ by the derived clause D$(<r)$ and the operator compatibility of [F5]; the residues $\pi_\lambda(b)$ over the surviving $b$ biject onto $\mathcal B(\lambda)$ by [F5]. These images span $V_A(\lambda)$ over $A$ because $U_A^-$ is spanned by the $G_\infty(b)$ and, by [F3] and step 6.1, $\pi_\lambda$ is surjective with the killed generators contributing zero.

**The module triple is integrally balanced (Y$(r)$).** Let $F_\lambda:=\bigoplus_{b:\pi_\lambda(b)\ne0}\mathbb ZG_\infty(b)v_\lambda$ inside $V_A(\lambda)\cap\mathcal L(\lambda)\cap\psi(\mathcal L(\lambda))$. It generates $V_A(\lambda)$ over $A$ by step 7.1 and its image in $\mathcal L(\lambda)/q\mathcal L(\lambda)$ is $\bigoplus_{\beta\in\mathcal B(\lambda)}\mathbb Z\beta$ by the bijection of residues, hence is a free generator group; the bar image is the corresponding free span in $\psi(\mathcal L(\lambda))/q^{-1}\psi(\mathcal L(\lambda))$, injective of the same rank. The chart generation criterion [F2](2), applied to $M=V_A(\lambda)$, $L_0=\mathcal L(\lambda)$, $L_\infty=\psi(\mathcal L(\lambda))$, gives integral balancedness in degree $\lambda-\alpha$ with $E_{\mathbb Z}=\bigoplus_{\pi_\lambda(b)\ne0}\mathbb ZG_\infty(b)v_\lambda$ and residue group $\mathbb Z\mathcal B(\lambda)$; with the induction hypothesis in lower degrees this is Y$(r)$. Uniqueness of the balanced lift identifies each $G_\infty(b)v_\lambda$ with the adapted module lift $G_\lambda(\pi_\lambda(b))$, which also proves (iv) in degree $\alpha$.

**Saturation and the adapted string bases.** The lifts $G_\lambda(\beta)$ for $\beta\in\mathcal B(\lambda)$ now form an $A$-basis of $V_A(\lambda)$ in every degree of height $\le r$, and by [F3] the ideals $J_{(i,n)}^A$ are generated by the images of the corresponding string ideal generators. Since each $F_i^{(n)}V(\lambda)$ is the $\mathbb Q(q)$-span of $\{\tilde f_i^n\beta:\beta\in\mathcal B(\lambda)\}$, its intersection with $V_A(\lambda)$ equals the $A$-span of the adapted lifts $\{G_\lambda(\beta):\beta\in\mathcal B(\lambda)\cap\tilde f_i^n\mathcal B(\lambda)\}$, which is exactly $J_{(i,n)}^A$; this proves the saturation identity and the displayed free decompositions of (iii) for the module, and the half decompositions were proved in step 5.2.

**Conclusion.** Steps 1.1 and 2.1 set up the induction and produce the balanced string ideals; steps 3.1 and 3.2 prove bar invariance and the gluing of string lifts; steps 4.1 and 5.1 construct the global half basis, its chart injections and X$(r)$; step 5.2 proves Z$(r)$ and the exact top-string transition (v); steps 6.1, 7.1, 8.1 and 9.1 prove Y$(r)$, the projection rule (iv), the module saturation and the adapted decompositions (iii) for both halves. The ranks in (ii) are the field dimensions computed by [F5] rank by rank, with the classical PBW identification supplied by [F8] and its stated Choice hypothesis; the dimension count is finite in each root degree because only finitely many compositions occur. This closes the induction in every degree and proves (i)-(v); the Choice use is confined to [C1].
